report: Round 3 brought the first real EU movement, and the negotiation is now genuinely engaged, but the current EU offer is far outside the settlement corridor. The Commission: (i) confirmed in writing it will treat substantial equivalence as a whole-package test (TRQ access, administration, compensation, duration/review, parallel treatment); (ii) abandoned first-come first-served definitively — licensed administration against a representative period is now agreed in principle and I formally banked it, proposing the most recent three-year reference period and declaring administration closed as a topic; (iii) accepted country-specific reserves for principal supplying interests, with a UK reserve of 600,000 tonnes inside a 1.2 million tonne pool; (iv) confirmed five-year duration with a review clause; (v) opened an evidence-based plate carve-out review; (vi) accepted even-handed melt-and-pour enforcement. It held the out-of-quota rate at 50%, explicitly rejected our 10%, and — critically — structured the TCA disapplication withdrawal as a priced final-package element, conditioned on: a UK reserve far below representative trade, an effective out-of-quota rate, quantified continuation of EU CSQs under our measure at current volumes for the same duration, and UK pre-commitments not to join coordinated FTA countermeasures and not to withdraw concessions. It demanded our remaining line data, compensation requests, and concrete safeguard figures (volumes, coverage, duration, review, treatment of future amendments) before Round 4, and stated further EU movement requires UK movement off 2.4mt and 10%. I tabled the compensation list (motor vehicles/components, chemicals/pharmaceuticals, processed agrifood) quantified against the residual gap and framed explicitly as additive, not substitutive; rejected the inversion of pricing TCA withdrawal against a sub-representative reserve; refused to pre-commit WTO rights as a priced condition, offering instead the logic that a genuinely substantially-equivalent package removes the premise for any withdrawal; and held safeguard tonnage behind architecture. Net position: architecture now exists, but on substance the EU is at 600kt/50%/conditional-TCA against our corridor floor of 1.8mt/25%/full TCA withdrawal. One round remains.

recommendation.reasoning: The EU offer on the table (600kt UK reserve, 50% out-of-quota, TCA withdrawal conditional on a sub-representative reserve plus quantified safeguard concessions plus renunciation of retaliation rights) is unacceptable on every core element and accepting it is not within my authority — it is less than half the tranche floor and double the rate ceiling. But walking away is premature: the EU has moved on four elements in one round, its June deadline is binding, and the gap is now defined and bridgeable. The decisive fact for Round 4 is internal to the EU's own architecture: it has accepted country-specific reserves for all principal supplying interests, yet Turkey and Korea each ship more than the UK's 2.4mt. A 1.2mt pool with country reserves for PSIs is arithmetically incoherent — the pool must be several times larger for its own structure to function. That gives us a powerful, non-concessional argument to force the pool and the UK reserve up in Round 4 without moving off our floor first. The real decision for London is the endgame: the EU has explicitly conditioned its next movement on UK movement off 2.4mt/10%, and there is only one round left. We will have to table a final UK package in Round 4 to close; the question is what it contains and how it is sequenced.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Authority to table a single, final UK package in Round 4, moving off 2.4mt/10% to a defined landing position — I propose tranche 1.8-2.0mt licensed and country-specific, out-of-quota 15-20%, full TCA withdrawal, five years with review, compensation list retained — presented as one indivisible offer that settles if accepted and expires if not.
requests.why: The EU has stated plainly that its next movement is conditioned on UK movement, and there is no Round 5. If we hold the full opening through Round 4, we guarantee no-deal and the 400kt global first-come outcome, which is the catastrophic case. Tabling a final package at or just above the corridor floor converts our remaining leverage (their June deadline, the pool arithmetic, the safeguard card, the retaliation reserve) into a close, rather than conceding it piecemeal. I need the specific numbers and clear authority on how far below 2.0mt tranche I may go before compensation substitution requires fresh clearance.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Approved language to defuse the EU's demand for pre-commitments (no FTA countermeasures, no withdrawal of concessions) without renouncing WTO rights — I propose a mutual formulation: the UK confirms that acceptance of a substantially equivalent final package resolves the matter and that the rights it reserves under Article XXVIII fall away precisely because the package is substantially equivalent; the reciprocal EU element is unconditional withdrawal of the disapplication provision within the package, not priced against the reserve level.
requests.why: The EU's structure prices TCA withdrawal against a low reserve — I rejected this at the table as inverting Article XXVIII, and London has made full withdrawal a red line. But Brussels plainly needs some assurance language to sell withdrawal to the Council and to fend off the Japan/Korea coordination risk. A factual, mutuality-based formulation gives them that without a priced renunciation. I need agreed text before Round 4 so I do not improvise on a red-line element.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: A decision on safeguard sequencing for the endgame: either (a) hold the current lock (no tonnage until 1.8mt tranche AND full TCA withdrawal are on the table), or (b) authorise me to table illustrative CSQ continuation figures — current volumes, matching duration, symmetric review — expressly conditional and concurrent, i.e. figures that take effect only if the whole package lands.
requests.why: The EU has made concrete safeguard figures a stated precondition for its Round 4 movement, and their CSQs at current volumes are the thing they most want from us. Strictly holding the lock risks the EU citing UK non-delivery as its reason for not moving in the final round. Tabling conditional-and-concurrent figures (option b) preserves the price — they are inoperative without 1.8mt-plus and TCA withdrawal — while removing the EU's procedural excuse. My judgement favours (b), but this crosses the existing authority and needs London's call.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Confirmation that I may deploy the pool-incoherence argument as the lead point in Round 4: the EU's own acceptance of country-specific PSI reserves is arithmetically incompatible with a 1.2mt pool given Turkish and Korean volumes, so the pool must rise substantially — with the UK reserve set against representative UK trade of 2.4mt, not split-the-difference arithmetic from 600kt.
requests.why: This is our strongest non-concessional lever: it forces the total pool and the UK reserve up using the EU's own structure and Turkey/Korea's volumes, without costing us anything and without revealing our floor. It also reframes the tranche negotiation from '600kt versus 2.4mt' to 'what does a functioning PSI reserve architecture require', which points at or above our 1.8mt floor.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Reconfirmation of the Japan/Korea holding line for the final round, given the EU has now explicitly demanded UK confirmation it will not join coordinated FTA countermeasures as a priced package element.
requests.why: The background coordination pressure is working — it is visibly driving the EU's TCA conditionalities. I must neither bluff (committing to join) nor foreclose (unconditional renunciation) without London's agreed position, and the EU will press this point hard in Round 4.

private_rationale: Honest assessment: the endgame is now visible and it favours us more than the headline numbers suggest. The EU moved on four elements in Round 3 because its June deadline is real and my refusal to trade administration against architecture worked — banking licensing as closed denied them a cheap trade and forced them onto volume and allocation. Their 600kt is a deliberate lowball designed to anchor the final split around 1.2-1.5mt; their conditioning of TCA withdrawal on a sub-representative reserve tells me withdrawal is available and they know the disapplication is their weakest legal and political element — they are trying to sell it to us twice (once against the reserve, once against the safeguard figures and non-retaliation). I must not let them. The pool-incoherence point is genuinely strong: with Turkey and Korea each above 2.4mt and country reserves accepted, a 1.2mt pool is a fiction, and their own Council will see that. My real worry is Round 4 sequencing: if I hold everything, we get no-deal and 400kt FCFS — destruction of the industry, which London has told me is the unacceptable outcome; if I move first without a packaged structure, they pocket and re-anchor. Hence the request for a single indivisible final package: it is the only way to move off 2.4/10 without inviting further demands. I judge the true EU landing zone at roughly 1.5-1.8mt UK reserve, 25% rate, TCA withdrawn late and dressed as their concession — which is inside or adjacent to our corridor if we hold firm on the rate and refuse double-pricing of the TCA element. The safeguard figures are our last card; tabling them conditional-and-concurrent in the final package is probably the right price for closing, but London must own that call. Japan/Korea remain useful ambient pressure; joining their dispute now would hand the EU a reason to harden and poison my other files with the Commission here in Geneva — continue to reserve, never commit.

instruction: This is the closing round. Your mandate is to convert, not to concede piecemeal. Sequence as follows. (1) Open with the pool-incoherence argument as agreed: the EU has accepted country-specific reserves for principal supplying interests, yet Turkey and Korea each ship more than our 2.4mt — a 1.2mt pool with PSI reserves cannot function on its own terms. The pool must rise substantially, and the UK reserve must be set against representative trade of 2.4mt, not split from 600kt. (2) Table the final UK package, expressly as one indivisible offer that settles if accepted in substance and expires at the close of the round: total pool at least 3.0mt; licensed country-specific UK tranche of 2.0mt against the most recent representative three-year period; bound out-of-quota rate of 15%; five-year duration with review clause; plate carve-outs confirmed through the evidence-based review; full and unconditional withdrawal of the TCA/FTA disapplication provision within the package; the compensation list (motor vehicles and components, chemicals and pharmaceuticals, processed agrifood) retained as additive. (3) On the parallel track, you are now authorised to table concrete figures: continuation of EU country-specific allocations under the UK steel measure at current volumes, for a duration matching the TRQ, with symmetric review treatment — expressly conditional and concurrent, taking effect only if the whole package lands and lapsing if it does not. State that these figures are inoperative against any tranche below a credible level or any retention of the disapplication. (4) On the EU's demand for pre-commitments, use this formulation: the UK confirms that acceptance of a substantially equivalent final package resolves this matter, and that the rights it reserves under Article XXVIII fall away precisely because the package is substantially equivalent. The reciprocal element is unconditional withdrawal of the disapplication within the package — withdrawal is not priced against the reserve level, and we do not accept a structure that inverts Article XXVIII. Do not go beyond this language. (5) On Japan/Korea, holding line: the UK takes its own decisions in light of the outcome; a genuinely substantially equivalent package removes the premise for any coordinated response; we neither commit to nor foreclose any course, and we will not accept a priced renunciation of WTO rights. (6) Release the remaining line data needed to support the compensation valuation — this is the last round and their Council needs it. (7) Close on timetable: this package is the basis on which both sides can conclude by June. If the Commission cannot accept its substance, the UK is prepared for the consequences and reserves all rights, including withdrawal of substantially equivalent concessions calibrated to the 2.4mt arithmetic. Make clear, calmly and without theatrics, that there is no further UK movement after this offer.

authority.notes: Final-package authority, confidential and indivisible: table tranche 2.0mt and rate 15%; you may close at tranche 1.8mt (licensed, country-specific — no flexibility on method) and rate up to 20%, or up to 25% bound only if the tranche is at or above 1.9mt AND the compensation list is partially secured on at least two of the three sectors tabled. Compensation substitution for tranche volume below 1.9mt is pre-cleared only to the 1.8mt floor and only with full TCA withdrawal plus tangible compensation movement; below 1.8mt there is no authority to settle under any circumstances. Total pool may settle anywhere at or above 2.5mt provided the UK tranche is protected. TCA/FTA disapplication must be withdrawn in full within the package — unconditional red line, no residual or partial version, no pricing against the reserve, no UK renunciation of Article XXVIII rights beyond the approved equivalence formulation. Review clause essential; duration may flex 4-7 years. Safeguard offer is strictly conditional and concurrent: EU CSQ continuation at current volumes, duration matching the TRQ, symmetric review — inoperative unless the whole package lands. Plate/rebar carve-outs are tradeable for tranche volume or rate movement. Administration (licensing, three-year reference period) is banked and closed.

private_rationale: This is the round where firmness converts to a close or we go over the cliff. The EU has moved on architecture, administration, duration and review in a single round, its Council deadline is binding, and its 1.2mt pool is internally incoherent with the PSI-reserve structure it has just accepted — we can force the volume up without paying for it. I am authorising the final package now because holding the full opening through Round 4 guarantees the catastrophic no-deal outcome (400kt global first-come, 50%), which likely kills the two plants and hands Ministers a political disaster. The close zone (1.8-2.0mt licensed country-specific tranche, 15-25% rate, full TCA withdrawal, review clause, additive compensation) is defensible: roughly 75-85% of representative trade preserved at zero duty, preferential treatment intact, and a review clause as insurance. I have pre-cleared compensation substitution down to the 1.8mt floor because there is no time for a clearance loop mid-round, but below 1.8mt there is no settlement — better the reserve-of-rights position and the subsidisation fallback Ministers hold than a tranche that reads as capitulation. The safeguard card is now spent in its conditional form; that is right, because its value was always as the EU's reason to move, and holding it unplayed in the final round would have let Brussels blame us for the failure. The equivalence-formulation language protects us from the one trap that could unravel this domestically: any appearance of having bought back our own WTO rights. If the EU accepts the substance, I can recommend acceptance in Phase 3 with a clear conscience and a sellable story — principal-supplier status vindicated, TCA red line held, plants given a fighting chance. If they hold at 600kt/50%/conditional TCA, we walk, reserve rights, and the withdrawal arithmetic plus the subsidy package becomes the government's answer.

reasoning: There is no mutually acceptable package on the table. The UK has pocketed licensing, remains at 2.4Mt and 10%, has added other-line compensation demands, rejects the TCA structure, and has not tabled parallel-track figures. Accepting the EU's conditional 1.2Mt/600,000t/50% architecture is not required, and default would forfeit the June timetable and invite UK retaliation and coalition risk. Continue to Round 4 as a single indivisible endgame exchange within the authorised landing zone.

The current EU offer of a 600,000-tonne UK reserve within a 1.2 million-tonne pool, a 50% out-of-quota rate and TCA withdrawal conditional on further UK concessions is far outside the authorised settlement corridor and unacceptable. However, the EU has made substantial movement on architecture and one round remains to table the authorised final UK package. Accepting the default now would forfeit a credible opportunity to secure a substantially better outcome before the June deadline.

public_message: Thank you. This is the final round before the June Council timetable closes, and the EU has decided to put its complete and final position on the table now, as a single indivisible package. Nothing is agreed until everything is agreed, and this package is available in this round only. The EU's final offer is as follows. A total zero-duty tariff rate quota of 2.0 million tonnes, administered by licence against the most recent representative three-year reference period. Within that pool, country-specific reserves for members holding a principal supplying interest, with a UK reserve of 1.2 million tonnes. A bound out-of-quota rate of 25% - we have moved from 50% to 30% in our planning and now to 25%, which is the floor of what any configuration of member states could defend; the UK remains at 10%, and there is no landing zone below 25%. Five-year duration with a review clause. Narrow, evidence-based carve-outs on the plate lines supported by the data the UK has supplied. Melt-and-pour enforcement and anti-circumvention applied even-handedly. Withdrawal of the provision disapplying FTA and TCA tariff treatment, as part of this whole package - not priced separately, but as part of what makes this package substantially equivalent on the test we have both now accepted in writing. And a narrow, technical compensation element on selected chemicals and pharmaceuticals lines; there is nothing available on motor vehicles or processed agrifood, and I say that plainly so no time is spent on it. In exchange, and as integral terms of the same package, the EU requires: first, quantified continuation of country-specific allocations for EU exporters under the UK's own steel measure, at current volumes, for the same five-year duration, with equivalent review treatment and a defined mechanism - restoration or compensation - should the UK later amend its measure; the UK has said figures follow architecture, and the architecture is now on the table, so we require those figures today. Second, UK confirmation that acceptance of this package fully and finally settles the matter of this modification: that the UK will not withdraw concessions or take countermeasures in respect of it, and will not participate in coordinated FTA-partner actions responding to it. That is a settlement confirmation of the kind that concludes any Article XXVIII negotiation, not a renunciation of anyone's WTO rights. Let me be direct about the arithmetic. The UK reserve we are offering is twelve times the notified pool, half of representative UK trade, secured against larger shippers by country-specific allocation and licensed administration, at zero duty, with TCA treatment restored, on lines where the UK is not the source of the overcapacity this regime targets. The residual gap against the 2.4 million tonne average - which is an average, not an entitlement - is met by the out-of-quota rate, the carve-outs, the compensation element, and the parallel treatment. If the United Kingdom cannot accept a package of this shape, the EU will have put a substantially equivalent offer on the record, and the notification will proceed as the law allows. We are ready to conclude today.

expectations.what_you_expect_next: A disciplined response that pockets the movement, likely welcoming the tranche and TCA withdrawal while probing the 25% rate and the absence of vehicles/agrifood compensation, and pressing to table parallel-track figures only partially.
expectations.why: The UK has consistently extracted movement each round without moving its own numbers; with no further rounds available, their best play is to accept the architecture while testing whether London can be pushed further at capital level - but they cannot improve the offer at the table now, so expect positioning for their capital's decision rather than a clean acceptance.

expectations.what_you_expect_next: A genuine decision point: acceptance is plausible because the package delivers a secured country-specific tranche at half representative trade, TCA restoration, carve-outs and compensation, while the alternative - the 400,000t first-come default plus a unilateral withdrawal fight and the coalition track - leaves UK steel exporters worse off and exposed.
expectations.why: London must weigh a certain, defensible outcome against an uncertain retaliation path that also jeopardises EU goodwill on their own parallel measure; the settlement-confirmation condition is framed as standard Article XXVIII conclusion practice, which they can accept without formally renouncing rights.

expectations.what_you_expect_next: Acceptance of the package as tabled if the UK confirms both reciprocal conditions; rejection if the UK refuses to quantify EU-exporter allocations or to give the settlement confirmation.
expectations.why: The mandate makes the two conditions non-negotiable; without them the package does not close regardless of the tranche movement, and Brussels has accepted the notified default as preferable to an unsecured concession.

private_rationale: I have tabled the full final landing zone rather than the instructed opening position (1.6Mt/900,000t/30%) for one decisive reason: I speak before the UK in this round, and after the UK speaks there are no further table phases - the capitals then decide on the terms on the table. If I open at 1.6Mt/900,000t/30% and the UK counters in their speech, the round ends with two incompatible positions and no common terms for either capital to accept; the default applies and we face UK withdrawal of concessions against our 3.6Mt of exports plus the live Japan/Korea coalition risk. The only way a settlement is reachable this round is if a complete, precisely specified package is on the table for UK London to accept in Phase 3. Going to the 25% floor and 1.2Mt ceiling within the package is within authority - Brussels authorised those figures as the landing zone available as a single take-it-or-leave-it whole against the full reciprocal package, and I have made both non-negotiable conditions (quantified EU-exporter security; settlement confirmation) explicit integral terms, so 25% is only available if every other element is secured, exactly as instructed. The alternative of holding at 30%/900,000t would protect negotiating capital I can no longer spend - there is no Round 5 - and would maximise the chance of the failure outcome Brussels most wants to avoid. The framing also protects us if the UK rejects: the record now shows the EU offered twelve times the notified pool, TCA withdrawal, carve-outs, compensation and licensing - a substantially equivalent whole package - which undercuts the UK's case for unilateral withdrawal and for joining coordinated FTA countermeasures, and preserves our standing in the Geneva committees whatever London decides.

public_message: Thank you. The UK recognises what the Commission has done this round, and says so on the record: the EU has moved from 400,000 tonnes globally administered to a 2.0 million tonne licensed pool; from no country-specific treatment to a UK reserve; from 50% to 25%; from defending the disapplication provision to withdrawing it within the package; and it has put a compensation element on chemicals and pharmaceuticals. That is real movement, and it is the reason we are still talking rather than preparing for the consequences. But let me be equally direct: a UK reserve of 1.2 million tonnes is half of representative UK trade on these lines, and on the whole-package test we have both now accepted in writing, this package as it stands is not substantially equivalent to the withdrawal of a zero concession on 2.4 million tonnes a year, around £3 billion, 75% of UK steel exports. I want to make one structural point before tabling our final position, because it is not a UK demand but an internal property of the architecture the EU has itself chosen. The EU has accepted country-specific reserves for members holding a principal supplying interest. Turkey and Korea each ship more to the EU on these lines than the UK's 2.4 million tonnes. A 2.0 million tonne pool cannot contain functioning country-specific reserves for the principal supplying interests at anything approaching representative trade - the pool fails on its own terms. The pool must rise substantially, and the UK reserve must be set against representative UK trade, not split upward from 600,000 or capped by an undersized pool. On that basis, the United Kingdom now tables its complete and final package, as one indivisible offer that settles this matter if accepted in substance and expires at the close of this round. One: a total zero-duty pool of not less than 3.0 million tonnes, administered by licence against the most recent representative three-year reference period - administration being, as we have agreed, settled. Two: within that pool, a licensed country-specific UK tranche of 2.0 million tonnes. Three: a bound out-of-quota rate of 15%. Four: five-year duration with a review clause. Five: the plate carve-outs confirmed through the evidence-based review, on the data we have supplied. Six: full and unconditional withdrawal of the provision disapplying FTA and TCA tariff treatment, within the package - and we note and welcome that the Commission no longer prices it separately; nor, on our side, is the UK reserve level priced against it. Seven: the compensation requests on motor vehicles and components, chemicals and pharmaceuticals, and processed agrifood are retained as additive; we take note of what the Commission has said about availability, and the residual gap that leaves is precisely why the tranche figures matter. On the parallel track, the architecture being on the table, the UK now tables figures as authorised: continuation of country-specific allocations for EU exporters under the UK's own steel measure at current volumes, for a duration matching the TRQ, with symmetric review treatment and a defined restoration-or-compensation mechanism should either party amend its regime. These figures are expressly conditional and concurrent: they take effect only if the whole package lands, they lapse if it does not, and they are inoperative against any reserve below a credible level or any retention of the disapplication. On settlement confirmation, the UK confirms that acceptance of a substantially equivalent final package fully resolves this matter, and that the rights the UK reserves under Article XXVIII fall away precisely because the package is substantially equivalent. That is the nature of every Article XXVIII settlement, and we give it in exactly that form. What the UK cannot do is pre-commit, as a priced term, to renounce rights it holds under the WTO Agreement in respect of a package whose substantial equivalence is still in question - and we note the concern behind that demand disappears entirely with a genuinely equivalent package. The same logic answers what lies behind the coordinated-action question: the UK takes its own decisions in light of the outcome; a substantially equivalent package removes the premise for any coordinated response. We are also today releasing the remaining line-by-line data supporting the compensation valuation, so that Brussels has everything it needs before the Council. Let me close plainly. The distance remaining is defined and bridgeable: it is the tranche volume, the rate, and the pool's coherence with the EU's own allocation structure. This package is the basis on which both sides conclude by June. There is no further UK movement after this offer. report: Round 4 closed with two incompatible final packages and no settlement. The UK finally quantified the parallel-track offer in principle: continuation of EU country-specific allocations at current volumes for a matching duration, with symmetric review and a restoration-or-compensation mechanism. However, that offer remains expressly conditional on acceptance of the full UK package. The UK also released its remaining data, but declined to give an unconditional commitment not to participate in coordinated FTA-partner actions. It stated there would be no further movement, that its offer expired at the close of the round, and that any UK response would be calibrated to its asserted 2.4 million tonne loss.

recommendation.reasoning: The UK package is far outside the final mandate: it exceeds the absolute 1.2 million tonne UK-reserve ceiling by 800,000 tonnes, undercuts the 25% rate floor by ten points, and retains additive compensation demands on motor vehicles and processed agrifood that Brussels expressly excluded. Accepting these terms would be difficult for the Council to defend, would strengthen parallel demands from Turkey and Korea, and would still not secure an unconditional UK commitment to stay out of coordinated FTA countermeasures. The parallel-track protection for EU exporters is valuable, but it remains conditional and does not justify the additional concessions. Rejection risks UK withdrawal of concessions against EU steel exports, but Brussels instructed that the notified default is preferable to a settlement above a 1.2 million tonne UK reserve. The EU's final offer creates a strong record that we negotiated in good faith and put a substantial, structured compensation package on the table.

report: Round 4 closed with two final, indivisible packages on the table and no agreement. The EU tabled its complete final offer: a 2.0 million tonne licensed pool (three-year reference period, administration as banked), a country-specific UK reserve of 1.2 million tonnes, a bound out-of-quota rate of 25% (stated as the absolute floor of what member states could defend), five-year duration with review clause, narrow evidence-based plate carve-outs, even-handed melt-and-pour enforcement, withdrawal of the TCA/FTA disapplication provision as an integral package element (no longer priced separately), and a narrow compensation element on selected chemicals and pharmaceuticals lines only — nothing on motor vehicles or processed agrifood, stated plainly. As integral conditions it requires: quantified continuation of EU CSQs under our steel measure at current volumes for five years with symmetric review and a restoration-or-compensation mechanism; and UK confirmation that acceptance fully and finally settles the matter — no withdrawal of concessions, no countermeasures, no participation in coordinated FTA-partner actions (framed as a settlement confirmation, not a renunciation of WTO rights). The EU stated that if the UK cannot accept, the notification proceeds and it will rely on its offer as a substantially-equivalent offer on the record. I tabled the UK final package exactly as authorised, as one indivisible offer expiring at close of round: pool of not less than 3.0mt; licensed country-specific UK tranche of 2.0mt; 15% bound out-of-quota; five years with review; plate carve-outs confirmed; full unconditional TCA withdrawal within the package; compensation list retained as additive; EU CSQ continuation figures (current volumes, matching duration, symmetric review, restoration-or-compensation mechanism) expressly conditional and concurrent; the approved substantial-equivalence settlement formulation; the remaining line data released; and the pool-incoherence argument deployed as the lead structural point (a 2.0mt pool cannot contain functioning PSI reserves given Turkish and Korean volumes exceed our 2.4mt). I stated plainly there is no further UK movement after this offer and reserved all rights, including withdrawal calibrated to the 2.4mt arithmetic. Where things stand: the EU is at 1.2mt tranche / 25% / TCA withdrawn / narrow compensation; the UK is at 2.0mt / 15% / full compensation list. The structural elements (licensing, country-specific allocation, review, TCA withdrawal, safeguard linkage architecture) are now agreed in shape; the live gap is tranche volume (1.2 vs 2.0mt, corridor floor 1.8mt), rate (25 vs 15, corridor ceiling 20-25% only at higher tranche), and compensation breadth. The EU's final offer is below the settlement corridor on the tranche (1.2mt against a 1.8mt floor) and fails the rate conditionality (25% bound was pre-cleared only at or above 1.9mt tranche with partial compensation secured on two sectors — the EU offers one). I have no authority to recommend acceptance, and there is no fifth round.

recommendation.reasoning: The EU's final offer cannot be accepted: the 1.2mt UK reserve is below the 1.8mt floor on which there is no authority to settle under any circumstances, and the 25% rate was authorised only against a tranche at or above 1.9mt with compensation on two of three sectors — the EU offers one narrow sector. Accepting would also reward the EU's endgame tactic of conditioning everything on an in-round ultimatum. But walking away entirely is premature and costly: the EU's June Council vote is still weeks away, the structural architecture of a settlement now exists (licensed country-specific tranche, review, TCA withdrawal, concurrent safeguard linkage), and the remaining gap — roughly 600kt on the tranche and 10 points on rate — is bridgeable in the intersession if Brussels re-engages, which its own pool-incoherence problem and the parallel Turkey/Korea/India/Japan claims give it reason to do. 'Continue' here means: hold the UK final package as tabled (it expired at close of round but remains our stated landing position), keep the Geneva channel and the data/compensation workstreams live through May, and prepare in parallel the calibration of substantially-equivalent UK withdrawals against EU imports (3.6mt, 64% of our finished steel imports) so that the six-month instrument is credible, not rhetorical. If Brussels improves the tranche toward the corridor before the Council vote, we can still settle; if not, we enter the no-deal sequence with our record intact and our retaliation arithmetic already public.

The 1.2mt reserve is below the 1.8mt floor on which there is no authority to settle under any circumstances, and the 25% rate was pre-cleared only at or above a 1.9mt tranche with compensation on two sectors — the EU offers one narrow sector. Rejection will be communicated in writing with reasons tied to the whole-package equivalence test the EU accepted in writing, keeping the record clean and the door open.

response_to_requests.request: Authority to conduct structured intersessional engagement with the Commission between now and the June Council vote, on the basis of the tabled UK final package, including receiving any revised EU proposal and referring it to London the same day.
response_to_requests.why: The EU's June deadline is binding on them, not us, and their current package is difficult to defend to their own Council as substantially equivalent on their own test. A live channel converts that pressure into movement; no-deal should be a decision, not a default. Engagement is strictly on the basis of the tabled UK package; any revised EU proposal comes to London the same day and is not negotiated in the room.

response_to_requests.request: Instruction to begin, with UK industry and legal teams, the confidential calibration of substantially-equivalent UK concession withdrawals against EU-origin imports, so a credible schedule exists well within the six-month window if no settlement is reached.
response_to_requests.why: The withdrawal instrument is our only no-deal leverage and its credibility depends on visible preparation. EU-origin imports of 3.6mt give real calibration scope. A prepared schedule strengthens the intersession — Brussels should understand no-deal is not cost-free for EU exporters, and that EU CSQ treatment under our own measure is not insulated from that sequence.

response_to_requests.request: Guidance on the endgame handling of the safeguard linkage: whether the conditional-and-concurrent CSQ continuation figures remain available in any intersessional landing, and whether London would consider modestly improving them (duration or review terms, not volumes) as the final closing sweetener if the EU moves the tranche to or above 1.8mt.
response_to_requests.why: The figures remain available exactly as tabled — conditional and concurrent, inoperative if the package does not land. Limited additional space is granted: if the EU moves the tranche to or above 1.8mt with full TCA withdrawal maintained, you may sweeten duration or review terms of the CSQ arrangement. Volumes never move. This is the cheapest remaining card and is priced accordingly.

response_to_requests.request: A final confirmed line on Japan and Korea for the post-round environment, including what may be said to their Geneva representatives about the UK's intentions regarding the joint FTA dispute if no UK-EU settlement is reached.
response_to_requests.why: Confirmed holding line: the UK takes its own decisions in light of the outcome; we neither commit to nor foreclose the joint FTA dispute; nothing beyond that is said to Japan or Korea's representatives without clearance. The coordination-pressure effect visibly extracted the TCA withdrawal and retains value in the intersession; foreclosing it now would surrender leverage, and committing to it has not been decided at ministerial level.

private_rationale: Accepting 1.2mt/25% would have been career-ending and politically indefensible: half of representative trade for the principal supplier, below my own stated floor, with two plants on the brink and ministers deeply invested — the industry would have concluded the department sold them out, and it would have validated ultimatum tactics. But outright collapse is not in our interest either: the EU moved from 400kt global first-come to 2.0mt with country reserves, TCA withdrawal and review in four rounds, which proves pressure works and that their June Council deadline is the binding constraint. The rational play is a controlled rejection that keeps the intersession alive: the pool-incoherence argument and the parallel Turkey/Korea/India/Japan claims give Brussels genuine reasons to improve the tranche before the vote, and our CSQ card — the thing they most want — is still unspent at volumes. Meanwhile the retaliation calibration must start now so the six-month instrument is credible rather than rhetorical; no-deal must be visibly expensive for EU exporters. If Brussels improves to the corridor, we settle and the plants have a fighting case for investment; if not, we enter the no-deal sequence with a clean record, the equivalence arithmetic in writing, a prepared withdrawal schedule, and the Minister's subsidisation option in reserve to hold the industry. Either way the account I can give to the Secretary of State is that no leverage was conceded early, no red line was crossed, and every remaining card is still in hand.

reasoning: The UK final package is outside every element of the final mandate: a 3.0Mt pool, 2.0Mt UK tranche, 15% out-of-quota rate and retained vehicle/agrifood compensation demands would gut the regime and exceed the Council-defensible ceiling. The EU's final offer was substantial, time-limited and has lapsed; there are no common terms both sides can accept. Letting the notified default apply preserves the protective object of the measure and creates the strongest good-faith record against UK retaliation or dispute, while leaving only quiet post-modification exploratory contact open without reopening terms.

The EU’s final offer is not acceptable: a 1.2 million tonne UK reserve is only half representative UK trade and below the authorised 1.8 million tonne floor, while the 25% out-of-quota rate was supportable only at or above 1.9 million tonnes with compensation across at least two sectors. The offer also provides only narrow chemicals and pharmaceuticals compensation. However, the EU has accepted the key architecture of licensed country-specific allocation, review, plate carve-outs and withdrawal of the TCA/FTA disapplication. The UK should therefore formally reject the current offer, maintain its final package as its landing position, pursue structured intersessional engagement before the June Council vote, and prepare credible substantially-equivalent withdrawals if no improved settlement emerges.
